summary.headline: Sejal Glass Q4 FY26 consolidated income rose over 72% YoY to INR 116.85 crores, with EBITDA margin at 17.5% and PAT at INR 11.42 crores.
summary.overview: Management reported strong Q4 and FY26 consolidated growth, with income crossing INR 400 crores for the year and margins expanding on product mix and operating leverage from integrated acquired facilities. The UAE business, over 70% of revenue, faces a regional slowdown and supply-chain disruption, though management guided to stable monthly run-rates of AED 10.2-10.5 million and an order book of about AED 60 million. India is being scaled up through the Glasstech acquisition, which reached EBITDA breakeven in the last month of FY26. Management guided FY27 consolidated revenue of about INR 500 crores and a 17.5-18% EBITDA margin, with new value-added products expected to contribute 5-7% of revenue this year.

segments.name: UAE business
segments.commentary: Monthly run-rate of AED 10.2-10.5 million; management expects about AED 31 million in Q1 FY27 and AED 35 million in Q2 if conditions improve. Q1 revenue guided to be in line with Q4. Over 70% of group revenue comes from UAE.

segments.name: India - Silvassa (existing)
segments.commentary: Capacity utilisation: tempering 64%, IG 30%, lamination 87%. Silvassa alone earns above 17-18% EBITDA margin. FY27 Silvassa revenue expected around INR 90 crores.

segments.name: India - Glasstech (Taloja and Erode)
segments.commentary: Utilisation: Taloja tempering 33%, IG 21%, lamination 8%; Erode tempering 13%, IG 3%. Glasstech FY26 revenue about INR 40 crores (post-acquisition operations from May/June 2025). Reached EBITDA breakeven in the last month; expects at least 10% EBITDA margin in Q1 FY27. FY27 expectation about INR 110 crores.

segments.name: New products (railway, fire, bullet-proof, digital, decorative)
segments.commentary: Railway tenders started (level 1 and level 2 orders won; bidding for Vande Bharat and AC coaches). Expected to be 2-3% of revenue from railway. Fire-rated glass (signed with Spain partner), standard and digital products to hit market in Q3 FY27; all new products 5-7% of FY27 revenue, 15-20% next year.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue target of about INR 500 crores (about 25% growth), with India about 40% (about INR 200 crores) and UAE about 60%.
Management said UAE revenue may grow about 20% in FY27 if the current situation holds; growth above 40% is possible if UAE improves.
FY27 consolidated EBITDA margin guided at 17.5-18%; UAE facade business could weigh about 1% on consolidated margin; raw material pass-through of 80-90% of cost increases expected.
India EBITDA margin targeted at about 15% for FY27.
India Q1 FY27 revenue expected to grow about 20% QoQ; India/UAE mix targeted at 60:40 this year and 50:50 thereafter.
Management expects no cash tax outgo in India for the next two years.
Glass prices rose about 7-8% in the last two months due to energy/gas cost; company says increases are passed through to customers.
Warrant call (about 4 lakh warrants, 75% balance) expected within 18 months, to be used for acquisitions.
capex_capacity: UAE: machines already ordered but delayed by one quarter due to geopolitical issues; expected installation in Q2 or Q3 FY27, funded by a mix of internal accruals and local/UAE bank debt.
Silvassa targets: tempering about 75%, IG above 50%, lamination 90-95% in FY27.
Taloja and Erode combined targets: tempering above 50%, IG and lamination together about 30%.
Second acquisition in India is under due diligence; management said it will take some time.
Taloja operations began June 2025 and Erode July 2025 after overhauling, re-engineering and labour set-up (about two quarters).
demand_pricing: UAE order book about AED 60 million; management said slowdown in real estate, with supply-chain disruption, but orders are in pipeline.
UAE strategy shifting toward Africa and other GCC markets; first European order won from India this quarter.
Demand drivers cited: premium and mid-income housing, office and data-centre leasing, infrastructure (airports, metro, rail, healthcare), and energy-efficiency rules favouring IG and laminated glass.
Segment shift in India from plain tempered glass to laminated and IG glass, driven by safety norms and architect specifications; India is about 60% plain tempered.
Saint-Gobain collaboration gives price advantage of about 4-5% via credit notes on project orders, plus special sizes that reduce wastage.
Non-real-estate (OEM) business is small but carries better margins; Glasstech gross margins similar to consolidated.

qa_highlights.question: What is the UAE outlook, Q1 run-rate and margin impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the UAE order book is about AED 60 million and monthly turnover is AED 10.2-10.5 million; Q1 could reach about AED 31 million and Q2 AED 35 million. Raw material cost increases are about 80-90% passed on; margin impact about 1-1.5% at EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: Are UAE debtors being paid on time?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said all payments and PDCs are being honoured on due dates, no customer has extended terms, and there are zero bad debts or delays so far.

qa_highlights.question: Why does India revenue look lower after including Glasstech?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said India ex-Glasstech was INR 63 crores in FY26; Glasstech's pre-acquisition figure included trading revenue, and consolidation, re-engineering and overhauling took about two quarters. Glasstech FY26 revenue was about INR 40 crores.

qa_highlights.question: What is the consolidated debt and debt reduction plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Consolidated debt is about INR 138 crores, of which about INR 70 crores is promoter-group funding and the rest is bank term loans on schedule. Some promoter loans were repaid in Q3 FY26.

qa_highlights.question: What is the gross margin path for standalone and consolidated?
qa_highlights.answer: Consolidated gross margins are better because UAE sales are mainly IG and laminated glass with no plain tempered glass. India gross margin is expected to improve as mix shifts, with COGS falling toward 61%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Saint-Gobain benefit?
qa_highlights.answer: Price advantage of about 4-5% through credit notes on project orders, plus special sizes and sales support from Saint-Gobain's pan-India team.

risks_watch: UAE real estate slowdown and supply-chain disruption; a worsening situation could reduce margins beyond the guided 1-1.5% impact.
Glasstech utilisation remains low (tempering 13-33%, lamination 8%); FY27 INR 110 crore target depends on ramp-up.
Execution risk on UAE machine installation (delayed one quarter) and new products (fire, railway, digital) launching in Q3 FY27.
Warrant call and second acquisition funding; debt rising from UAE capex.
Glass price increases of about 7-8% from energy costs; pass-through depends on order timing.
Monitor quarterly UAE turnover against AED 31 million (Q1) and AED 35 million (Q2) guidance, and Glasstech EBITDA margin of at least 10%.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on FY27 growth and margins, but cautious on UAE, where management repeatedly tied outcomes to the geopolitical and supply-chain situation. Some answers on margin, gross-margin and India numbers were loose or revised mid-answer, so the guidance should be treated as provisional.
